<thought>We need the number of aromatic carbons in the molecule, but we have no structural description. The most direct way is to obtain the 13C NMR spectrum of the sample and count the signals that fall in the typical aromatic carbon chemical shift range (≈110–160 ppm). This will give the number of distinct aromatic carbon environments, which for most molecules corresponds to the total number of aromatic carbons unless symmetry reduces the count. We'll request the carbon NMR spectrum and then count the aromatic-region peaks.</thought>
